questions.text: Give the register map: offset, width, reset value and access of every register (ID, DATA, CRC, CTRL), and the read value of an undefined offset.
questions.default: 0x00 ID RO 0x43524333; 0x04 DATA WO 0x00000000 (write absorbs a word, read 0); 0x08 CRC RO 0x00000000 (readback of ~crc_state); 0x0C CTRL WO 0x00000000 (bit 0 clears, self-clearing); undefined offsets read 0 and ignore writes
questions.reason: spec.md names registers and reading back but gives no offsets; this map is the simplest layout that fits the four named functions
questions.answer: 0x00 ID RO 0x43524333; 0x04 DATA WO 0x00000000 (write absorbs a word, read 0); 0x08 CRC RO 0x00000000 (readback of ~crc_state); 0x0C CTRL WO 0x00000000 (bit 0 clears, self-clearing); undefined offsets read 0 and ignore writes

questions.text: Should the readback be the finalized CRC (final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF applied) or the raw internal state?
questions.default: Finalized CRC: an empty stream reads 0x00000000 and the result matches the standard CRC-32 used by Ethernet
questions.reason: spec.md asks for the standard Ethernet CRC-32, which includes the final XOR
questions.answer: Finalized CRC: an empty stream reads 0x00000000 and the result matches the standard CRC-32 used by Ethernet

questions.text: In what order are the bytes of each 32-bit word absorbed?
questions.default: Byte 0 is wdata[7:0], processed first, each byte LSB first (little-endian, reflected order as in Ethernet)
questions.reason: spec.md gives no byte order; little-endian LSB-first matches the reflected CRC-32 byte stream definition
questions.answer: Byte 0 is wdata[7:0], processed first, each byte LSB first (little-endian, reflected order as in Ethernet)

questions.text: Should the CRC be reset by the CPU reset button only, or also by CTRL clear?
questions.default: Both: CPU reset (C12) and CTRL bit 0 set crc_state to 0xFFFFFFFF
questions.reason: spec.md asks for a clear command and a reset with the CPU button; both are named, so both are kept
questions.answer: Both: CPU reset (C12) and CTRL bit 0 set crc_state to 0xFFFFFFFF

questions.text: Is the reset synchronous (state clears on a clock edge while rst_n is low) or asynchronous?
questions.default: Synchronous, with the reset pin C12 as the only reset source
questions.reason: Synchronous reset is the usual choice for a single-clock design and gives clean timing on the reset path
questions.answer: Synchronous, with the reset pin C12 as the only reset source

questions.answer: Active high, led[k] = CRC readback bit k
